edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant provides these preliminary responses to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production, subject to completion of request-specific responses and confirmation of applicable requirements before service.

1. PRIVILEGE AND PROTECTION. Defendant does not agree to produce material protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or other applicable protection. Any objection and any withholding on that basis will be identified in the applicable request-specific response as required by governing law.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control as required by applicable rules and any governing agreement or court order. Request-specific responses will identify any objections, whether responsive materials are being withheld on those grounds, and the applicable production timing.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent responsive documents are withheld on privilege or protection grounds, Defendant will provide the information required by applicable rules and any governing agreement or court order.
4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct these responses as required by applicable rules or court order.

edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. This draft is for discussion only and is not intended for service as complete responses. Before service, Defendant will complete a reasonable inquiry and provide request-specific responses by the applicable deadline, including verification to the extent required by governing law. Each response will identify applicable objections with specificity, state whether responsive materials are withheld on those grounds, and identify definite production dates, as required by governing law.

2. PRODUCTION. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control as required by applicable rules and any governing agreement or court order. Subject to agreement and any governing requirements, Defendant proposes rolling production beginning within 14 days after responses are due and completion within 30 days after responses are due. Request-specific responses will state definite production dates. Any necessary extension will be agreed in writing or addressed by court order.

3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent responsive documents are withheld on privilege or protection grounds, Defendant will provide the information required by applicable rules and any governing agreement or court order. Subject to those requirements and agreement, Defendant proposes an initial log within 14 days after the first production, supplemental logs every 14 days during production, and a final log within 14 days after production is completed.

4. SUPPLEMENTATION. Defendant will supplement or correct these responses as required by applicable rules or court order.

5. PRESERVATION AND ESI PROTOCOL—PROPOSAL FOR DISCUSSION. Defendant is seeking confirmation of preservation measures for potentially responsive materials and will provide confirmation once verified. Subject to agreement and governing requirements, Defendant proposes searchable PDF or TIFF production with extracted text or OCR and load files as appropriate; native production for spreadsheets and other files where necessary to preserve usability; reasonably necessary metadata, including custodian, source filename, relevant dates, email sender and recipients, subject, and attachment relationships where available; and preservation of parent-child document-family relationships. The parties should confer on sources, custodians, date ranges, collection and search methods, deduplication, secure transfer, and treatment of privileged family members before finalizing the protocol.
